products.name: dbt (Data Build Tool)
products.description: Open-source + cloud data transformation framework; SQL-first, modular, tested, version-controlled. Ecosystem-dominant with 4000+ packages. Fivetran merger (Oct 2025) creates 600M ARR data infrastructure platform.
products.positioning: Build data pipelines like software engineers build apps—modular, tested, version-controlled with interactive lineage and automatic refactoring.

products.name: SQLMesh
products.description: High-performance open-source data transformation framework. 9x faster than dbt Core, features column-level lineage, virtual environments (free in dev), incremental-by-default models, smart plan execution. Acquired by Fivetran (Sept 2025), donated to Linux Foundation (March 2026).
products.positioning: Modern data transformation with virtual environments and intelligent planning—optimize cost and speed without complexity.

products.name: Great Expectations
products.description: Python-first data quality framework (open-source + GX Cloud). Community-driven (11k+ Slack) with flexible approach to testing, validation, and profiling. Series B $40M (total $65M). Perpetual open-source under Apache 2.0.
products.positioning: Create a shared point of view on data quality with a flexible, community-driven toolset. Python-first with orchestrator integration and automated actions.

products.name: Soda
products.description: AI-native data quality monitoring platform (SaaS + Soda Core open-source). Advanced ML with peer-reviewed research (NeurIPS, JAIR, ACML). YAML/SQL-friendly approach. Record-level anomaly detection. €11.5M Series A (2023), €12.9M Series B (2024), total $40.9M.
products.positioning: Stop data incidents before they hit production with AI-native detection, automatic fix recommendations, and collaborative data contracts.

products.name: Monte Carlo
products.description: Cloud-only data observability platform with unified data + agent observability. ML-driven anomaly detection, #1 G2 leader (8 quarters). Forrester study: 375% ROI, 80% reduced downtime. Series D $135M (2024, $1.6B valuation), total $236M.
products.positioning: Agent trust platform that unifies data and agent observability to monitor, troubleshoot, and improve production AI systems.

products.name: Elementary
products.description: Data observability & control plane (dbt-native, open-source + cloud). Code-first observability with AI-first governance. Unifies quality, governance, observability, discovery. Seamless dbt integration via dbt package hub. Well-funded ($10M+ seed/Series A).
products.positioning: Trusted data control plane for the AI era—unified governance, quality, observability, and discovery in code, powered by AI agents.

notes: Phase C extraction complete for competitors-data-transformation-quality leaf. Coverage: 6 products (dbt, SQLMesh, Great Expectations, Soda, Monte Carlo, Elementary) spanning transformation (dbt, SQLMesh) and quality/observability (GX, Soda, MC, Elementary). Feature assessment focuses on 14-16 most relevant features per product from the 110-feature taxonomy; mapped against MetroGraph's HCI-first, graph-based, database-agnostic positioning. Key competitive insights: (1) dbt & Monte Carlo are high-threat due to ecosystem dominance & market leadership; (2) MetroGraph's wedge is HCI focus (metro-map visualization + AI parity) + database agnosticism vs vendor lock-in; (3) Transformation tools (dbt/SQLMesh) focus on versioning/lineage; quality tools (GX/Soda/MC/Elementary) focus on alerting/observability; Elementary is the only other dbt-native platform; Soda differentiates on AI/YAML-friendly approach. Sources: T0 official pages, T1 documentation/GitHub, T2 G2/Forrester, T3 practitioner comparisons. Market context: dbt-Fivetran merger (600M ARR, mid-late 2026), SQLMesh donated to Linux Foundation (March 2026), Monte Carlo unicorn ($1.6B, $236M raised), Soda $40.9M Series AB.
